target: AArch64 QEMU virt with PCI VirtIO sound and WAV backend
command: QEMU_VIRT='-machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -m 1024 -device ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=/tmp/zeal-morse-final.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' python3 scripts/check-compat.py --probe-demo-morse-code
checks: Launched the unchanged stock /Demo/Sound/MorseCode.ZC and rendered its Morse table.
Injected a short key-down/key-up pulse; the key was sampled through the stock MessageScan/CharGet path and caused the Morse dot tone.
QEMU WAV captured 10584 stereo frames at 44.1 kHz (0.24 s); 19404 samples were nonzero and peak amplitude was 7000.
Shift-Escape exited MorseCode and returned to the graphical terminal; 40+2 evaluated to 42 and zstatus reported failed=0.
scope_note: Verifies MorseCode keyboard timing, sound generation through QEMU VirtIO sound, and terminal recovery. Live UTM and Raspberry Pi sound output remain unverified.
